source.title: When Pruning Meets Interpretability: Preserving Sparse Autoencoder Robustness in LLMs
source.authors: Suchit Gupte; Xue-Ru Zhang; M. Khalili

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper conceptually tests whether SAE feature representations remain reliable under post-hoc pruning, using SAEBench measures rather than the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the superposition hypothesis as background but does not test overlapping feature directions, feature sparsity or importance transitions, polysemantic neurons, or one-dimensional feature geometry. Its own relevant results measure how fixed pretrained SAEs behave after weight pruning. Perplexity comparisons for layer-wise sparsity allocation and cited results from other work are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses fixed pretrained SAEs as a measuring tool and reports how pruning methods change their SAEBench scores. Its question is whether an SAE trained on a dense model still works after weight pruning. That bears on the pruning method and on SAE transfer, not on whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of the model's representation (V5). It also does not test V1–V4 or V6; superposition is cited only as background. Its finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, for a fixed SAE, pruning-induced degradation is governed by covariance-weighted perturbation energy. MAGNITUDE pruning degrades SAE behaviour most, while WANDA and SparseGPT preserve it better. Core metrics understate the damage seen on SCR/TPP. Middle layers are most vulnerable, which they attribute to accumulated upstream perturbation rather than local energy. A preliminary layer-wise sparsity schedule lowers perplexity.
record.recipe_differences: The cited original is a toy-model study of superposition geometry; this paper instead prunes pretrained LLM weights and evaluates fixed SAEs with SAEBench metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning method and layer depth alter outcomes; the paper also evaluates multiple sparsity levels (25%, 40%, 50%) and ablation thresholds for SCR/TPP.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed SAE trained on a dense LLM degrades on SCR/TPP (up to 60–80% in worst layers) and Core metrics after 50% MAGNITUDE pruning. Under WANDA/SparseGPT it degrades less. Middle layers are most sensitive. Absorption changes are small and mixed in sign.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE validity transfers to a weight-pruned model only when the pruning-induced activation perturbation energy is small; activation-aware pruning preserves SAE behaviour better than magnitude pruning.

record.problems: The experiments cover four model-SAE pairs and hold SAE weights fixed. Pythia-70m absorption results are excluded as unreliable; Mistral-7b has SAE coverage at only three layers. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. The authors describe layer-wise sparsity allocation as preliminary and do not explain middle-layer sensitivity theoretically.
record.rows_left_out: Kept the middle-layer Table 1 results and the selected aggregate Table 2 feature/causal metrics. Omitted Table 1 early and late layer-group entries, Table 2 Core metrics and SCR full-ablation values, and per-layer Table 4–6 values; these are omitted to stay within 60 rows and because the selected measures most directly bear on SAE feature integrity and interventions. Figure 4 threshold curves and Table 3 perplexity results are not separate evidence for V5 canonicality.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or polysemantic neurons.
Uses pretrained SAEs but does not test distributed features or SAE recovery as evidence of superposition.
Completeness, canonicality, and stability across SAE seeds or sizes are untested. The authors list retraining SAEs on the pruned model and comparing features as future work.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V5. However, robustness of a fixed SAE to weight pruning measures tool transfer under model perturbation, not whether SAE features are the model's canonical units, so no verdicts are given. Row values check against Tables 1–2. Several reader states were inconsistent: for example, absorption falls after pruning in gemma aggregates, and Mistral SCR rises under WANDA. Superposition (Elhage et al.) appears only as introductory background.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test toy-network feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
It does not test whether feature competition for representational capacity causes neuron polysemanticity or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
It does not study alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
It evaluates pretrained SAEs on LLM activations but does not test whether model features are distributed across neurons or establish sparse SAE-recoverable features as evidence for superposition.

Tests retention of fixed pretrained SAE behavior after unstructured weight pruning. It does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the dense model's representation.
The paper does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: WANDA and SparseGPT at 50% sparsity on aggregate gemma-2-2b and mistral-7b measurements
reader_labels.reason: The reported absorption and SCR values are near or better than dense baselines in these settings, supporting conditional retention of SAE feature behavior (C2-C3, C5-C6, C11-C12, C14-C15, C26-C30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MAGNITUDE pruning and middle layers; also aggregate TPP results across the tested models
reader_labels.reason: Feature/intervention metrics often deteriorate after pruning, particularly for MAGNITUDE pruning in middle layers; activation-aware methods also show declines on several measures. The results establish robustness only conditionally, not canonicality (M1-M3, M5-M9, C4, C7, C13, C16, C19-C24, C28, C31-C33).
